name: Muse Code
description: Meta's terminal coding agent, launched in beta with Muse Spark 1.2; it runs a main agent alongside persistent background subagents.
strengths: Approval modes and an OS sandbox on by default
Subagents, skills, hooks and MCP; event log lets sessions resume after a crash
Headless `muse exec`, session protocol and TypeScript SDK
weaknesses: Muse Spark 1.3 scores 14.6% on Terminal-Bench 4.0
Workflows unavailable on some builds/platforms; Windows lacks voice input and session messaging
Default contributor mode lets Meta train on your content (can be turned off)

pricing.notes: Four subscription tiers (Everyday, High 5x, Power 20x, Maximum 80x; Power adds Muse Wonder Full) or pay-as-you-go per token with a Meta Model API key; prices shown only at checkout.

notes: Notable: appears on the official Terminal-Bench leaderboard (tbench.ai, Terminal-Bench 4.0 — the only version tbench.ai currently shows), best rank #32; only five distinct agents are listed there, so every one is top-10. Scores are TB 4.0 resolution rates (best per model across reasoning efforts), fetched 2026-10-14 — not comparable with older Terminal-Bench 2.x figures. Default model muse-spark-1.2; the changelog names Muse Spark 1.2 and 1.3 and allows any model id 'on the same provider', hence 'vendor'. No licence or repo stated, so openSource=false.

name: Mistral Vibe
description: Mistral's open-source command-line coding assistant, launched with Devstral 2 and usable in IDEs over the Agent Client Protocol.
strengths: Apache-2.0
Agent profiles (ask, plan, accept-edits, auto-approve) and a per-run --max-price cap
Programmatic mode for scripting
weaknesses: Requires a Mistral API key; Mistral models only
Officially targets UNIX

pricing.notes: Billed at Mistral API rates (e.g. Devstral 2 $0.40/$2.00 per M tokens after its free period).

name: Google Antigravity
description: Google's agentic development platform: a desktop app for running several agents, an agentic IDE, a CLI and a Python SDK.
strengths: Free for individual developers
Model menu spans Gemini, Claude Opus/Sonnet 5.5 and GPT-OSS 120B
Agents work across editor, terminal and browser and report via artifacts
weaknesses: Gemini 4 Argon only on Ultra/Enterprise and not in the IDE
Claude 5.5 models need a paid (non-trial) Pro plan or higher

pricing.notes: Individuals $0 with weekly rate limits; Google AI Pro/Ultra raise limits and add a credit pool; Business from $30/seat/mo or pay-as-you-go via Google Cloud.

notes: Notable: frontier-lab developer (Google). Launched as a free public preview alongside Gemini 3. Model list also includes Claude Opus 4.6 (not in models.json); Sonnet 4.6, Opus 4.6 and GPT-OSS 120B are scheduled for removal 2026-11-02.

name: Factory Droid
description: Factory's model-agnostic software development agent, available in a desktop app, CLI and SDK with cloud and local background agents.
strengths: Model-agnostic: frontier and open-weight models, including custom ones
Topped the Terminal-Bench 1 (Core v0.1.1) leaderboard at launch with 58.8% (Opus 4.1)
Cloud 'Droid Computers' for remote agents on Plus and up
weaknesses: Not on the current Terminal-Bench 4.0 leaderboard
Subscriptions start at $20/mo

pricing.notes: Pro $20/mo; Plus $100/mo; Max $200/mo; Teams $60/mo + $40/seat; Business/Enterprise contact sales.

notes: releaseDate from Factory's 2025-09-25 post saying Droid is 'available across all interfaces today'. Its 58.75% (Opus 4.1), 52.5% (GPT-5), 50.5% (Sonnet 4) were on the older Terminal-Bench Core v0.1.1 board and are not on tbench.ai's current 4.0 leaderboard, so not in scores. factory.ai now redirects to factory.com.

name: mini-SWE-agent
description: A minimal open-source coding agent from the SWE-agent team: a roughly 100-line agent class whose only tool is bash, used widely as a benchmark baseline.
strengths: Works with any model via LiteLLM, OpenRouter, Portkey and more
Tiny, readable codebase with a linear message history
Runs locally or in Docker/Podman, Singularity, bubblewrap and other sandboxes
weaknesses: Bash is its only tool; no IDE integration
Best Terminal-Bench 4.0 result is 19.1% (Gemini 3.8 Flash)

pricing.notes: Free software; you pay your model provider.

notes: Notable: appears on the official Terminal-Bench leaderboard (tbench.ai, Terminal-Bench 4.0 — the only version tbench.ai currently shows), best rank #29; only five distinct agents are listed there, so every one is top-10. Scores are TB 4.0 resolution rates (best per model across reasoning efforts), fetched 2026-10-14 — not comparable with older Terminal-Bench 2.x figures. releaseDate is the earliest GitHub release (v1.0.0.dev4); the repo was created 2025-06-28. Now at v2.

name: Kiro
description: AWS's spec-driven agentic IDE, also available as a CLI and on the web, with an Auto router or a manually chosen model.
strengths: Spec-driven workflow: requirements, design and tasks before code
Pick Auto or a specific Claude, GPT-5.6 or open-weight model
IDE, CLI, web and ACP-compatible IDEs share one credit pool
weaknesses: Third-party harnesses routing outside Kiro's interfaces are not permitted
Credit cost varies by model

pricing.notes: Free 50 credits; Pro $20; Pro+ $40; Pro Max $100; Power $200 per user/month; add-on credits $0.04.

notes: supportedModels partial: GPT-5.6 variants (unspecified), GLM-5 and Qwen3 Coder Next are offered but don't map to models.json ids. Launched in preview 2025-07-14.

name: Gemini CLI
description: Google's open-source terminal agent for Gemini models, with Search grounding, file and shell tools, and MCP support.
strengths: Apache-2.0 open source
Free tier with a Google account: 60 requests/min, 1,000/day
Non-interactive mode with JSON/streaming output and a GitHub Action
weaknesses: Gemini models only
Not on the Terminal-Bench 4.0 leaderboard

pricing.notes: Free tier with Google sign-in or Gemini API key (1,000 requests/day); usage-based billing beyond via API key or Vertex AI; Code Assist Standard/Enterprise licences.

notes: Notable: frontier-lab developer (Google). Google also ships an Antigravity CLI (separate entry).

name: OpenCode
description: An open-source coding agent for the terminal, desktop and IDE that connects to 75+ model providers, including local models.
strengths: MIT licence; about 213k GitHub stars
75+ providers via Models.dev, plus sign-in with GitHub Copilot or ChatGPT Plus/Pro
Free models included; parallel sessions and shareable session links
weaknesses: Desktop app still in beta

pricing.notes: Free with included free models or your own keys; paid Zen (curated models) and Go offerings — prices not on the homepage.

notes: Repo moved from sst/opencode to anomalyco/opencode; company id 'anomaly' is a guess from the GitHub org name — no company page fetched. releaseDate is the earliest GitHub release (0.0.45).

name: Claude Code
description: Anthropic's agentic coding tool: reads a codebase, edits files and runs commands, available in the terminal, IDE extensions, a desktop app and the browser.
strengths: #1 and #2 on Terminal-Bench 4.0 (Opus 5.5 64.8%, Sonnet 5.5 61.8%)
Runs on terminal, VS Code, JetBrains, desktop app, web and mobile
Subagents, skills, hooks and MCP integration
Third-party providers supported on the CLI, VS Code and JetBrains
weaknesses: Not open source: the public repo is 'All rights reserved', under Anthropic's Commercial Terms
Most surfaces require a paid Claude plan or Console account

pricing.notes: Pro $20/mo ($17/mo annual), Max 5x $100/mo, Max 20x $200/mo, Team/Enterprise; or Claude Console account billed at API rates.

notes: Notable: appears on the official Terminal-Bench leaderboard (tbench.ai, Terminal-Bench 4.0 — the only version tbench.ai currently shows), best rank #1; only five distinct agents are listed there, so every one is top-10. Scores are TB 4.0 resolution rates (best per model across reasoning efforts), fetched 2026-10-14 — not comparable with older Terminal-Bench 2.x figures. releaseDate is the limited research preview announced with Claude 3.7 Sonnet. supportedModels='vendor' per Anthropic's docs (Claude models, incl. via Bedrock/Vertex-style third-party providers), although tbench.ai also lists Claude Code runs on non-Anthropic models (GLM-5.3, GLM-5.3-Flash, Qwen3.8-Max-0902) — included in scores since they are official leaderboard rows.

name: goose
description: An open-source, Rust-built AI agent with a desktop app, CLI and API, working with 15+ model providers and 70+ MCP extensions.
strengths: Apache-2.0, under the Linux Foundation's Agentic AI Foundation
15+ providers incl. Anthropic, OpenAI, Google, Ollama, OpenRouter, Azure, Bedrock
Can use existing Claude, ChatGPT or Gemini subscriptions through ACP

pricing.notes: Free software; you pay your model provider or use an existing subscription.

notes: Originally from Block (not mentioned on the current repo page). releaseDate is the earliest GitHub release (v0.9.0); repo created 2024-08-23.

name: Cline
description: An open-source coding agent available as a VS Code extension, JetBrains plugin, CLI, desktop app and SDK, not tied to any one model provider.
strengths: Apache-2.0 open source
Providers include Anthropic, OpenAI, Google, OpenRouter, Bedrock, Vertex, Groq, Ollama, LM Studio and any OpenAI-compatible API
Free for individuals: pay only for inference
weaknesses: JetBrains extension listed under the Enterprise tier on the pricing page

pricing.notes: Open-source tier free; bring your own provider keys. Enterprise custom pricing.

notes: releaseDate is the earliest GitHub release (v1.0.4); repo created 2024-07-06.

name: OpenHands
description: An open-source, self-hostable platform for running coding agents, with a web UI, CLI and Docker sandboxes.
strengths: MIT licence
Bring your own model: works with any LLM
Can also orchestrate Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI, OpenCode and other ACP agents
weaknesses: Cloud pricing not stated on the repo

pricing.notes: Self-hosted is free with your own model keys; optional OpenHands Cloud/Enterprise (pricing not on the repo).

notes: The repo README now brands the product 'Agent Canvas' (agent-canvas CLI, v1.27.1 image); the GitHub repo moved from All-Hands-AI/OpenHands to OpenHands/OpenHands. releaseDate is the earliest GitHub release (0.6.1, when the project was OpenDevin).

name: Aider
description: An open-source AI pair-programming tool for the terminal that edits code in your local git repo.
strengths: Apache-2.0 open source
Connects to almost any LLM, including local models
Works from inside editors, accepts images and web pages as context, supports voice
weaknesses: Terminal-first; no first-party IDE extension

pricing.notes: Free software; you pay your model provider.

notes: releaseDate is the earliest GitHub release (v0.5.0); repo created 2023-05-09.

name: GitHub Copilot
description: GitHub's AI coding assistant, with agent mode in VS Code, Visual Studio, JetBrains, Eclipse and Xcode, the Copilot CLI and a cloud agent that opens pull requests.
strengths: Agent mode and Copilot CLI on every plan, including Free
Models from Anthropic, OpenAI, Google, xAI, Moonshot and Microsoft
Cloud agent turns assigned issues into pull requests (Pro and up)
weaknesses: Usage metered in AI credits; cost varies by model
Delegating to third-party agents (Claude, Codex) needs Pro+ or Max

pricing.notes: Free $0; Pro $10; Pro+ $39; Max $100 per month (credits at $0.01); Business/Enterprise for orgs.

notes: releaseDate is Copilot's general availability (2022-06-21); Copilot CLI entered public preview Sept 2025 and went GA 2026-02-25 per GitHub's changelog. supportedModels left [] because the plans page names model families (Claude Haiku/Sonnet/Opus, GPT-5/6, Gemini Flash, Grok, Kimi, MAI-Code-1.1-Flash) without exact versions. GitHub is a Microsoft subsidiary; not a frontier lab under the rule. copilot-cli repo licence is not an OSI licence (GitHub reports NOASSERTION).

name: Codex
description: OpenAI's coding agent, available as the open-source Codex CLI, an IDE extension, a desktop app and Codex Cloud on the web.
strengths: #3 on Terminal-Bench 4.0 (GPT-6 Astra and GPT-6.1 Sol, both 58.2%)
CLI is open source (Apache-2.0)
Included in every ChatGPT plan from Free upward
Custom providers via any Responses-API-compatible gateway, incl. Amazon Bedrock
weaknesses: Custom providers must expose a Responses API endpoint; Chat Completions-only endpoints are unsupported
Free and Go plans limited to lighter use on GPT-6 Luna

pricing.notes: ChatGPT Free $0, Go $8, Plus $20, Pro from $100 ($100/$200/$500), Business $20/user/mo annual; API-key use billed at API rates.

notes: Notable: appears on the official Terminal-Bench leaderboard (tbench.ai, Terminal-Bench 4.0 — the only version tbench.ai currently shows), best rank #3; only five distinct agents are listed there, so every one is top-10. Scores are TB 4.0 resolution rates (best per model across reasoning efforts), fetched 2026-10-14 — not comparable with older Terminal-Bench 2.x figures. releaseDate null: Codex CLI launched 2025-04-16 per launch coverage (TechCrunch) and the GitHub repo was created 2025-04-13, but no OpenAI page confirming the date could be fetched (openai.com returned 403). Open source applies to the CLI; the app and cloud are proprietary.

name: Grok Build
description: xAI's coding agent: a terminal TUI, headless mode and Agent Client Protocol integration, plus an app-building mode in the Grok web and mobile apps.
strengths: Interactive TUI, headless (`grok -p`) and ACP modes
Accepts any custom model via a base URL in ~/.grok/config.toml
Available on every Grok plan since 2026-08-19
weaknesses: Grok 4.7 scores 37.6% on Terminal-Bench 4.0, well behind Claude Code and Codex
No open-source licence or repo published

pricing.notes: Included on every Grok plan since 2026-08-19 (Early Beta was SuperGrok Heavy only); XAI_API_KEY sign-in for non-browser environments. No prices on the docs page.

notes: Notable: appears on the official Terminal-Bench leaderboard (tbench.ai, Terminal-Bench 4.0 — the only version tbench.ai currently shows), best rank #21; only five distinct agents are listed there, so every one is top-10. Scores are TB 4.0 resolution rates (best per model across reasoning efforts), fetched 2026-10-14 — not comparable with older Terminal-Bench 2.x figures. releaseDate null: x.ai's 2026-08-19 post says Grok Build was introduced 'in July' as an Early Beta without giving a day. x.ai/build itself returned 403. 'web' covers the in-chat app builder on web/iOS/Android described in the same post.

name: Cursor
description: An AI code editor with a CLI and cloud agents, offering models from OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, SpaceXAI and its own Composer models.
strengths: Broad model menu: Grok, Claude, Gemini, GPT, GLM, Kimi, Muse and Composer
Desktop editor, CLI, cloud agents, Slack and GitHub PR review
Plans from a free tier up to $200/mo Ultra
weaknesses: Third-party models need Premium ($30/mo) or higher, billed at API list price on top of the plan
Plus ($8) plan is Grok-only
Not on the Terminal-Bench 4.0 leaderboard

pricing.notes: Free $0; Plus $8 (Grok only); Premium $30 (adds third-party models at API list price); Super $100; Ultra $200; Teams $30+/user; Enterprise custom.

notes: Notable by the frontier-lab rule only if SpaceX ownership counts: Cursor says it was acquired by SpaceX (post dated 2026-08-14) after an April partnership with SpaceXAI, and its footer still reads Anysphere, Inc. — kept a separate company id; reviewer should decide whether notable applies. releaseDate null: no launch date found on a Cursor page. Models list omits GPT-6-family models; not mapped: Composer 2.5, Kimi K2.7 Code, GPT-5.x Codex variants and others absent from models.json. Not Notable: Anysphere is not one of the five frontier labs, whatever its ownership, and Cursor is not on the Terminal-Bench leaderboard.

name: Zed
description: An open-source code editor with a built-in agent panel that runs hosted or bring-your-own-key models and external agents such as Claude Agent and Codex CLI.
strengths: Open source (GPL-3.0-or-later, some Apache-2.0)
Personal plan free forever with your own keys or external agents
BYOK providers include Bedrock, Anthropic, Google, OpenAI, OpenRouter, Ollama and GitHub Copilot
weaknesses: Zed-hosted model usage billed at API list price plus 10%

license.name: GNU GPL v3 or later (Apache-2.0 components where marked)

pricing.notes: Personal $0 with own keys; Pro $10/mo with $5 tokens then usage; Business $30/seat/mo.

notes: releaseDate null: no launch date for Zed's agent features found on a Zed page. license.kind 'restricted' used for copyleft (commercial use allowed).

name: Warp
description: An agentic development environment built around a terminal, with a built-in coding agent, an agent CLI for any terminal and cloud agents.
strengths: Client is open source (AGPL-3.0; UI crates MIT)
Switch models per task or run different models in parallel
Can host third-party CLI agents (Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI)
weaknesses: BYO API keys/custom endpoints on Business and Enterprise; Free tier BYO inference is footnoted

license.name: GNU AGPL v3 (UI framework crates MIT)

pricing.notes: Free $0; Build $20/mo (incl. $20 agent usage); Max $200/mo; Business $50/user/mo; Enterprise custom.

notes: supportedModels is partial: the pricing page names Claude Opus 5, 'GPT-5.6' (variant unspecified, so unmapped), Gemini 3.1 Pro, GLM 5.2, Kimi K3 'and more'. releaseDate null; earliest release in the open-source repo is 2026-04-29, which is not the product launch. AGPL is copyleft (kind 'restricted', commercial use allowed); spdx 'AGPL-3.0' as GitHub reports it — -only vs -or-later not stated.

name: Kilo Code
description: An open-source coding agent for VS Code, JetBrains, the CLI and a cloud agent, with access to 500+ models.
strengths: MIT licence
500+ models, switchable mid-task; BYOK or local via Ollama/LM Studio
Provider rates with no markup on the Kilo Gateway (5% credit purchase fee)
weaknesses: Cloud agent compute billed separately per second

pricing.notes: Platform free for individuals with own keys or pay-as-you-go gateway credits; optional Kilo Pass $19/$49/$199 per month; Teams $15/user/mo.

notes: releaseDate null: earliest GitHub release visible (v1.0.25, 2026-02-23) postdates repo creation (2025-03-10), so it is not the launch.

name: Junie
description: JetBrains' coding agent, available as a CLI, inside JetBrains IDEs, and in GitHub Actions and GitLab CI/CD.
strengths: Works with any model you choose: 10+ via BYOK, plus local models
Free Junie Lite model with every JetBrains account
Uses IDE code intelligence across multiple projects
weaknesses: Regular use recommended on AI Ultimate ($25/user/mo)

pricing.notes: Free Junie Lite or BYOK at provider rates; AI Pro $8.33/user/mo (10 credits); AI Ultimate $25/user/mo (35 credits).

notes: Open-source status unconfirmed: a public repo exists but GitHub reports no recognised licence (NOASSERTION); set openSource=false. releaseDate null: none on the product page.

name: Qwen Code
description: Alibaba's open-source terminal coding agent, with a desktop app, editor plugins and SDKs, supporting Qwen, OpenAI, Anthropic, Gemini and local models.
strengths: Apache-2.0
Any third-party provider or local model (Ollama/vLLM); switch at runtime
Desktop app, VS Code/Zed/JetBrains plugins, TypeScript/Python/Java SDKs
weaknesses: Web UI and daemon mode are experimental

pricing.notes: Free software; costs depend on the chosen provider.

notes: releaseDate null: repo created 2025-06-26; earliest GitHub release visible is v0.0.1-alpha.14 (2025-08-01), so earlier alphas likely existed.

name: Devin Desktop
description: Cognition's AI IDE (formerly the Windsurf Editor), with the local Devin agent, delegation to cloud Devin and an agent command center.
strengths: Runs Devin Local, the same harness as Devin CLI
Hands tasks to cloud Devin and manages all agents in one place
Adaptive router or a chosen model (SWE-2, Claude, GPT)
weaknesses: Exact model list and prices not confirmed on fetched pages

pricing.notes: Free, Pro, Teams and Enterprise with daily/weekly quotas; prices not confirmed.

notes: windsurf.com now 308-redirects to devin.ai/desktop. The rename date (2026-06-02) comes only from secondary sources (Coder docs), so releaseDate is null. Devin itself (cloud agent, vendor picks the model) is an agent, not a harness.
